prose:
Every proof result says how much it can be trusted. A clause is proved only when every input of a finite declared
domain was checked and none broke it; that evidence is formal. When the domain is too large or cannot be
enumerated, a clause that holds on every sample is evidenced, never proved, and its evidence is empirical. One
counterexample makes the clause violated. A clause whose if-part no input satisfies is vacuous, because it proves
nothing. A clause that rejects none of the planted bugs is weak, because it rules out no mistake. A recorded
production run that breaks a clause makes it violated, even when it was proved on the model.

decisions.question: Which evidence label does a violated clause carry?

options.label: Formal from the exhaustive check, empirical from samples or production runs
options.consequence: The label says where the counterexample came from; a production run that breaks a clause the model already broke is labeled empirical.

options.label: Always empirical
options.consequence: A counterexample found by enumerating the whole domain is reported with the same weight as one found by sampling.

decisions.question: Which evidence label does a weak clause carry when it held on every input?

options.label: None
options.consequence: A weak clause never counts as formal or empirical evidence in the receipt, like a vacuous one.

options.label: Keep formal or empirical
options.consequence: The receipt shows formal evidence for a clause that rules out no bug.
